plan.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): how to protect muscle while losing weight, and why protein quality matters as well as quantity
plan.angle: Title: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): 3 Ways to Protect Your Muscle'. 1) A protein food at each meal, from a variety of sources (fish, eggs, dairy, legumes, poultry), 'unless your clinician has told you to limit protein'. 2) Muscle-strengthening at least 2 days a week, per activity guidelines. 3) Eat enough overall, with no extreme restriction. Cite the SURMOUNT-1 DXA paper and the 2025 joint advisory instead of Yahoo. Close with the prescriber line.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): 3 Ways to Protect Your Muscle #shorts
plan.why: Muscle is our best cross-platform GLP-1 topic (98 YT views, 61 IG reach, 238 IG views). The playbook asks to rebuild the muscle carousel as a Short, and this how-to angle is new. | fact-check: This is our strongest pillar (muscle). The SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy (Look et al., 2025, Diabetes Obes Metab) reports roughly 3:1 fat-to-lean loss on tirzepatide. Use the paper's exact percentages and its substudy population (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a related condition, without type 2 diabetes). The 'protein quality, not just quantity' hook comes from a Yahoo Health lifestyle piece. The evidence that protein type preserves muscle on GLP-1s is thin, so don't make it a claim. Base the habits on the 2025 joint nutrition advisory for GLP-1 users (ACLM/ASN/OMA/TOS), which covers adequate protein and resistance training. For strength training, use the guideline wording: 'at least 2 days a week' (US Physical Activity Guidelines / NHS). Keep the kidney caveat. In habit 3, add an eating-disorder-safe line: no extreme restriction.

factcheck.summary: Content check of the Short 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): 3 Ways to Protect Your Muscle'. All four sources exist and say what the script claims. SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy (Look et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2025, doi 10.1111/dom.16275, PMC11965027): 160 of 2,539 participants, adults with BMI ≥30 or ≥27 plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes, scanned at week 72. Tirzepatide group: −21.3% weight, −33.9% fat mass, −10.9% lean mass. Placebo group: −5.3%, −8.2%, −2.6%. About 75% of the weight lost was fat in both groups, so the 'mostly fat' framing is correct. The joint advisory (Mozaffarian et al., Obesity 2025;33(8):1475–1503, doi 10.1002/oby.24336) lists adequate protein and strength training to preserve lean mass among its priorities. CDC (updated Dec 20, 2023) gives the exact wording '2 or more days a week that work all major muscle groups'. NHS (reviewed May 22, 2024) lists resistance bands and bodyweight exercises. Safety is handled well: there's a limit-protein caveat for people told to restrict it (e.g. kidney disease), an 'extreme restriction isn't the goal' line, the prescriber line, and no dosing or stopping advice. The script runs about 140 words. There are only minor wording fixes: say the results are averages, don't overstate that the 3 habits are proven to protect muscle on tirzepatide, and attribute the advisory correctly. The Wiley and DOM publisher pages returned 403 to direct fetch. I confirmed both DOIs through PMC, CiteDrive and indexed citations.
